iHealth PT9L Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer

title_content.content: To verify the accuracy and repeatability of the Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer, according to requirement in ATSEM 1965-98.

paragraph_content.content: DUT:
device under test, iHealth PT9L Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer in this study
RCT:
Reference clinical thermometer in this study
2.1 Intended use

The Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer is intended for the intermittent measurement of body temperature from the forehead skin surface on people of all ages. It can be used by consumers in the household environment and by healthcare providers.
Device description

The iHealth PT9L Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer is hand-held, reusable, battery operated device, which can measure human body temperature on the skin temperature on one's forehead. Its operation is based on measuring the natural thermal radiation from the central forehead. Put the probe of the thermometer is onto the skin of a patient’s central forehead. Pressing the activation button to start the measurement of proposed infrared radiation. The electrical signal read out from the detector is fed to the circuit for amplification and calculation. The final measured temperature will be appeared on a LCD display.

2.3 Contraindications
It is not recommended for people whose forehead has local lesions, such as inflammation, trauma, recent surgery, etc..
2.4 See the user guide for how to operating the device.
Electronic thermometer is used as reference clinical thermometer, using a water bath to verify the laboratory accuracy of the reference thermometer  before and after the test.

Step 1: Sequence the Participants and sign Serial numbers for them according to participant time.
Step 2: using a water bath to verify the laboratory accuracy of the reference thermometer.
Step 3: The supervisor take the DUT, prepare to take measurement for the first subject.
Step 4: Perform three consecutive measurement procedures with the time interval no more than 1 min between each reading. And record the test results.
Step 5: Take one measurement with the RCT to get oral temperature, and record the test results.
Step 6: Repeat step 3 to step 5 to complete all the measurements of the participants.
Note, in this step, the participants signed with odd numbers were measured with DUT first and then with RCT, participants signed with even numbers were measured with RCT first and then with DUT.
Step 6.using a water bath to verify the laboratory accuracy of the reference thermometer again.
